workflow: status: confirm running:true and extension_connected:true; if not, call start and ask the user to enable the extension.
session: name the task once (one task = one visible tab group).
navigate: open the URL; newTab:true keeps earlier pages.
snapshot: read the @e refs and choose a target.
click or fill: act on an @e ref (preferred) or a CSS selector.
wait: wait for a concrete result (text, text_gone, or selector).
snapshot, read_page, or screenshot: verify behavior, not just appearance.
close_session: close the tabs this task opened; borrowed tabs stay open.
hint: Core tools are listed directly. browser_tools {query:"..."} searches; browser_tools {tool:"name"} returns its arguments and an example; browser_call {tool, args} runs a long-tail tool.

groups.name: tabs
groups.about: Find, borrow, activate, or close tabs

groups.name: read
groups.about: Reader mode, search, extract, console, network, and dialogs

groups.name: interact
groups.about: Real pointer, keyboard, select, hover, scroll, drag, and upload

groups.name: history
groups.about: Reload, go back, or go forward

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Open a URL in the user's real browser. Reuses the task tab by default; newTab:true keeps the current page open. Pass group_title on the first call so the task tabs are labeled together.

url.description: Absolute URL including the scheme, e.g. https://example.com

newTab.description: Open in a new tab instead of reusing the current task tab

group_title.description: Human-readable tab-group label, set once per task

tools.summary: Open a URL in the real browser.
tools.signature: navigate({ url: string, newTab?: boolean, group_title?: string })

tools.name: activate_tab
tools.description: Bring the current task tab to the front so the person can see it. Set focus_window:true to also focus the browser window. Use before request_human and whenever the human needs to look at the page.
tools.summary: Bring the task tab to the front; optionally focus the window.

tools.name: history
tools.description: Reload the current tab, or move back or forward in its history. The bound is the tab's own history, so back at the first entry returns a daemon error.
tools.summary: Reload, go back, or go forward in the current tab.

tools.name: find_tab
tools.description: Select a tab already owned by this task, matched by host. Use active:true to borrow the tab the user is currently viewing. If it fails, the page is not open in this task: call navigate with newTab:true.

active.description: Borrow the foreground tab the user is viewing

tools.summary: Reselect a tab this task owns, by host; active borrows the foreground tab.

tools.name: list_tabs
tools.description: List the tabs owned by this task, with tabId, url, title, active, groupTitle and borrowed.
tools.summary: List the tabs this task owns.

tools.name: list_browser_tabs
tools.description: List every tab in the browser across windows, without attaching or focusing. Use before attach_tab.
tools.summary: List every browser tab without attaching.

tools.name: attach_tab
tools.description: Attach an existing tab (from list_browser_tabs) to this task. Borrowed tabs are spared by close_session. This does not focus the tab, so the user keeps their foreground page.
tools.summary: Claim an existing tab as borrowed; it stays open after close_session.

tools.name: close_tab
tools.description: Close the current task tab. Use only when closing that page is intended.
tools.summary: Close the current task tab.

tools.name: close_session
tools.description: Finish the task: close the tabs it opened. Borrowed user tabs stay open. Call when results are saved or the user asks to clean up. Returns the number closed.
tools.summary: Close the tabs this task opened.

tools.name: snapshot
tools.description: Page map: the accessibility tree with @e refs for clicking and filling. Call after navigate and after every page change; refs go stale. Default returns JSON {url, title, tree}; format:"aria" returns text with max_chars and cursor. On large or still-loading pages, use format:"aria" with max_chars, snapshot(ref), or wait for a selector first; JSON can be big or slow. Next: click or fill with a ref.

ref.description: Optional @e ref to narrow the snapshot to one subtree

cursor.description: Continuation cursor from a previous ARIA response

tools.summary: Read the page map with @e refs.
tools.signature: snapshot({ ref?: string, format?: "json" | "aria", max_chars?: number, cursor?: string })

tools.name: read_article
tools.description: Reader mode: strip navigation, sidebars, comments, and ads, then return the article as clean Markdown with title, byline, and date. Use it to quote, summarize, or save an article without page chrome. On pages without an article container, it falls back to the winning text block.
tools.summary: Reader mode: strip page chrome and return clean article Markdown.

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search the page text and return matching @e refs; narrow a large page with snapshot(ref).
tools.summary: Search page text and return matching @e refs.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Read the page's main text when you need content rather than structure. Keep max_chars near the amount you need; a much larger cap can add scan time. Use start to page through long documents. For clicking, use snapshot; for embedded documents, pass the frame handle from snapshot.frames.
tools.summary: Read the page text.
tools.signature: read_page({ max_chars?: number, start?: number, frame?: string })

tools.name: wait
tools.description: Wait for a concrete page condition after an action: visible text, text that disappears, or a selector. Any one ends the wait; timeout_ms is 500-60000 and defaults to 10000. Set snapshot:true to get the page map in the same call. Next: snapshot or read_page to confirm.

text_gone.description: Visible text to wait to disappear

frame.description: Wait for an embedded document, or pass "any"

snapshot.description: Include a snapshot when the condition matches

tools.summary: Wait for a concrete page condition.
tools.signature: wait({ text?: string, text_gone?: string, selector?: string, frame?: string, timeout_ms?: number, snapshot?: boolean })

tools.name: click
tools.description: Click an element by @e ref from the latest snapshot (preferred) or a CSS selector. This is a synthetic click; if the page ignores it, use browser_tools to find mouse_click. Next: wait, then snapshot or read_page to verify.
tools.summary: Synthetic click on a ref or selector.

tools.name: mouse_click
tools.description: Real pointer click (mousedown/mouseup) at the element center. For sites that ignore synthetic clicks.

focus_emulation.description: Enable focus emulation first, required for background tabs

tools.summary: Real pointer click; use when a synthetic click is ignored.

tools.name: key_type
tools.description: Type text into the focused element as real keystrokes (Input.insertText). Focus the field first with mouse_click when click does not, then call this for search boxes with autocomplete, masked inputs, or editors that reject set values.

focus_emulation.description: Enable focus emulation for a background tab

tools.summary: Type real keystrokes into the focused element.

tools.name: hover
tools.description: Move the pointer over an element to open hover menus, tooltips, and preview cards. Pairs with a following snapshot (or read_page) that sees the revealed content.

focus_emulation.description: Enable focus emulation for a background tab

tools.summary: Hover to open menus, tooltips, or preview cards.

tools.name: select_option
tools.description: Choose options in a native <select> by value or visible label, firing input and change events. For custom dropdown widgets, click to open the menu and click the option instead. With no value and no values, returns the available options.

selector.description: @e ref or CSS selector for the <select>

value.description: One option value or visible label

values.description: Several options for a multiple select

tools.summary: Choose native <select> options by value or label.
tools.signature: select_option({ selector: string, value?: string, values?: string[] })

tools.name: set_checked
tools.description: Set a checkbox, radio, switch, or ARIA checkbox/switch to a given state, including indeterminate handling. Use when click would toggle an already-correct state or the control is a styled label.
tools.summary: Set a checkbox, radio, switch, or ARIA control.

tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scroll to an element, to visible text, to the page top/bottom, or one screen up/down. Use it to load lazy content before snapshot, or to bring a target into view. When several inputs are given, target wins over text, and to/direction scroll the page.

selector.description: @e ref or CSS selector to scroll into view

text.description: Visible text to find and scroll to

to.description: Scroll the page to an edge

tools.summary: Scroll to an element, text, page edge, or one screen.
tools.signature: scroll({ selector?: string, text?: string, to?: "top" | "bottom", direction?: "up" | "down" })

tools.name: drag
tools.description: Drag from one element to another using HTML5 drag events or a pointer sequence. The result states which mode ran; a pointer drag reports dispatched without verification, so confirm the outcome with snapshot.

from.description: @e ref or CSS selector for the drag source

to.description: @e ref or CSS selector for the drop target

tools.summary: Drag one element onto another; verify with snapshot.

tools.name: fill
tools.description: Set an input, textarea, or rich-editor value in one step. Pass an @e ref from the latest snapshot or a CSS selector. For autocomplete, masked inputs, or keystroke-driven editors, use browser_tools to find key_type. Next: wait, then verify.
tools.summary: Set an input or editor value.

tools.name: send_keys
tools.description: Dispatch keyboard keys to the focused element: Enter, Escape, Tab, ArrowDown, or Mod+A / Control+C. Use focus_emulation for background tabs. Verify page state afterwards; dispatch alone does not prove submission.

focus_emulation.description: Enable focus emulation for a background tab

tools.summary: Send Enter, Escape, Tab, or Mod+A to the focused element.
tools.signature: send_keys({ keys: string, repeat?: number, focus_emulation?: boolean })

tools.name: evaluate
tools.description: Run page JavaScript and return {type, value}. Wrap statements or async work in an IIFE: (() => {...})() or (async () => {...})(). Keep returned data compact.
tools.summary: Run page JavaScript; wrap statements in an IIFE.

tools.name: cdp
tools.description: Raw Chrome DevTools Protocol passthrough for actions the higher-level tools cannot express. Target.activateTarget is refused; use Page.bringToFront, or Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled for background input.
tools.summary: Raw CDP passthrough; Target.activateTarget is refused.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Visual check of the tab or one element; returns the image plus a file path. Use it for layout and appearance; use snapshot or read_page for content. PNG by default; format:"jpeg" with quality for smaller captures.

selector.description: Optional @e ref or CSS selector for one element

path.description: Optional absolute output path; omit to use the daemon default directory

tools.summary: Visual check of the tab or one element.
tools.signature: screenshot({ format?: "png" | "jpeg", quality?: number, selector?: string, path?: string })

tools.name: save_as_pdf
tools.description: Render the current tab to PDF and return the saved file path.
tools.summary: Render the current tab to PDF and return its path.
tools.signature: save_as_pdf({ paper_format?: "letter" | "legal" | "a4" | "a3" | "tabloid", landscape?: boolean, scale?: number, print_background?: boolean, path?: string })

tools.name: highlight
tools.description: Draw a temporary box around an element in the real page so the person can see exactly where to look or click. Use it with request_human for sign-in fields, consent buttons, and any hand-off. action:"show" returns a highlight_id; action:"clear" removes it. Highlights expire after duration_ms (default 30 s, max 120 s).

selector.description: @e ref or CSS selector to highlight

tools.summary: Draw a temporary box around an element for the user.
tools.signature: highlight({ action?: "show" | "clear", selector?: string, highlight_id?: string, duration_ms?: number })

tools.name: capture_page
tools.description: Bookmark the current tab as agent-friendly Markdown with YAML frontmatter (url, title, captured_at, tags) plus a links section. One bounded DOM walk, no extra network traffic. Writes <YYYYMMDD-HHmmss>-<slug>.md and appends a line to index.jsonl in the capture directory (WEBBRIDGE_CAPTURE_DIR or ~/.webbridge/captures).

tags.description: Tags stored in the frontmatter and index line

screenshot.description: Also save a PNG next to the Markdown; off by default for speed

tools.summary: Save the tab as Markdown with frontmatter and links.
tools.signature: capture_page({ dir?: string, tags?: string[], screenshot?: boolean, max_chars?: number })

tools.name: extract
tools.description: Extract structured data with CSS selectors: matching elements become JSON objects. Without fields, each item returns text plus href for links, src for images, or value for inputs. With fields, each item returns only the named sub-selectors/attributes. Use for tables, cards, lists and search results; cheaper than a full snapshot when you know the markup.

selector.description: CSS selector for the repeated items, e.g. "table tbody tr"
Selector inside each item; omit for the item itself

attr.description: Read this attribute instead of text

include_empty.description: Keep items whose fields are all empty

tools.summary: Extract repeated elements as JSON with optional fields.
tools.signature: extract({ selector: string, fields?: object[], max_items?: number, include_empty?: boolean })

tools.name: console
tools.description: Read console output and page errors for the current tab. Call action:"start" before the interaction, then action:"read" (optionally clear:true) to collect log/info/warn/error/debug plus uncaught errors and unhandled rejections. Bounded to 200 entries; action:"stop" removes the hook.

clear.description: With read, clear messages after returning them

tools.summary: Start, read, or stop console and error capture.

tools.name: dialog
tools.description: Inspect or answer a JavaScript dialog (alert/confirm/prompt). A blocking dialog stalls other commands, so use action:"accept" or "dismiss" when one is open. text supplies the prompt answer.

text.description: Prompt answer for accept, when the dialog asks for text

tools.summary: Inspect or answer an alert, confirm, or prompt.

tools.name: upload
tools.description: Set files on a file input. Files must be absolute local paths readable by the daemon.
tools.summary: Set absolute files on a file input.

tools.name: network
tools.description: Capture network requests for the current tab. cmd:"start" begins capture, "list" lists requests (filter by URL substring), "detail" returns headers/body for one requestId, "stop" ends capture (and drops response bodies, so read details first).
tools.summary: Start, list, detail, or stop network capture.
tools.signature: network({ cmd: "start" | "stop" | "list" | "detail", filter?: string, requestId?: string })

tools.name: status
tools.description: Preflight. Report whether the local daemon and the browser extension are connected, plus the active toolset. Call this first. Browser tools start the daemon lazily when needed; if extension_connected is false, ask the user to enable the extension, then retry once.
tools.summary: Check the daemon and extension before starting.

tools.name: start
tools.description: Start the local daemon if it is not running, then report status. Safe to call repeatedly. Browser tools also do this lazily; start is only for prewarming.
tools.summary: Start the daemon if it is not running.

tools.name: session
tools.description: Name this task; its pages form one visible tab group. Call once at the start of a multi-step task (e.g. "compare-phones"). Skip it for a single quick page.
tools.summary: Name the task and its tab group.

tools.name: batch
tools.description: Run several tool calls in one round-trip and return per-step results. Use for tight sequences (fill → click → wait) and flash-sale timing, where extra calls add latency. Steps stop at the first failure unless stop_on_error is false. Images are not returned; use the screenshot tool directly.

steps.description: Up to 40 steps, executed in order

stop_on_error.description: Stop after the first failure, default true

tools.summary: Run up to 40 steps in one round-trip; stops at the first error.

tools.name: request_human
tools.description: Hand control back to the person and wait: sign-in, 2FA, captcha, consent, or any step that needs their judgment. The extension opens a small prompt with the reason; the call returns when they press Continue or the timeout passes, then re-check the page. Never use this to confirm payment; stop at the order page and let the person finish.

reason.description: One short line shown to the person

instructions.description: What they should do, in their language

tools.summary: Hand control to the person for sign-in, 2FA, captcha, or a decision.
tools.signature: request_human({ reason: string, instructions?: string, timeout_ms?: number })

args.instructions: Finish the login, then press Continue.

tools.name: browser_tools
tools.description: The rest of the browser suite: tabs, extraction, network, console, files, PDF, JavaScript, batch, and human handoff. No arguments returns the workflow and tool groups; query searches names and descriptions; tool returns one tool's full arguments and an example. Use it before browser_call.

query.description: Words to match in tool names or descriptions

tools.summary: The rest of the browser suite: tabs, extraction, network, console, files, PDF, JavaScript, batch, and human handoff.

tools.name: browser_call
tools.description: Run a long-tail tool by name with its argument object. Call browser_tools {tool} first to get the arguments. Core tools are listed directly; prefer them.
tools.summary: Run a long-tail tool by name with its argument object.
